issues.note: PR OPEN and NOT MERGED, branch 000henrik/mar-537-runner-standalone-flake cut from master at ad2b1bd after confirming that commit is master's tip, so there is no reconciliation merge to read. A FLAKY BLOCKING GATE, AND THE CAUSE IS AN ORDERING BUG RATHER THAN SLOWNESS. tests/runner-standalone.test.ts asserts on the runner's first four startup lines and reached them by polling for runner.json. That file is a STRICTLY EARLIER EVENT than the lines: runner/main.ts writes it at line 349, immediately after listenOnEndpoint resolves, and prints `listening on`, `store:` and `contracts:` at lines 367-372 afterwards. So the wait ended, by construction, at a moment when the child might not have printed any of them — and under load, where it is the PARENT's own stdout `data` callbacks that run late, it regularly had not. The 100ms poll interval is why this looked rare: the three console.warn calls land microseconds after the write, so only a parent descheduled inside that window loses them. THE OBSERVED SIGNATURE WAS THEREFORE A LIE ABOUT ITS OWN SUBJECT: `expected '[runner] standalone start: node=24.18…' to contain '[runner] listening on'` is a truncated string blaming the built artifact for a race in the harness observing it, on a commit (PR #75) that changed one block comment in electron/capture.ts. THE FIX IS THE ISSUE'S OWN FIRST PREFERENCE, and it SUBSUMES the old wait rather than sitting beside it: waitForLine reads the child's output until `[runner] contracts: <artifact>/contracts` appears, and because runner.json is written before that line is printed, the file is present whenever the line has arrived. The marker is the `contracts:` line rather than `listening on` because that is the line the SECOND test reads — a wait ending on an earlier one would leave that assertion racing exactly as the first pair used to. THE ISSUE'S SECOND PREFERENCE IS BUILT IN: both failure paths carry the child's whole captured output, its exit code and its signal, so the next occurrence is diagnosable from a CI log. A child that EXITS is reported the moment it exits rather than at the deadline, because the interesting cases — an unsuitable host exiting 78, a missing module exiting 1 — are all fast, and spending 60 seconds on them would bury the cause under a timeout that reads like slowness. The beforeAll hook timeout moved 90s -> 150s for one reason: comfortably above the build plus waitForLine's own 60s, so a genuinely slow start is reported by a sentence that names the line, the exit code and the output rather than by vitest's hook timeout, which names none of them and is the failure this issue is about. NOT SKIPPED AND NOT RETRIED IN-PROCESS, per the issue: the artifact starting under plain Node on a tree containing only itself is MAR-497's whole proof. Assertions are unchanged; runner/ is untouched. EXIT EVIDENCE, exactly as the issue specifies: 20 consecutive solo runs of the file, 20 passed / 0 failed, while `pnpm exec vitest run tests` ran concurrently in a second shell — and that concurrent full suite was itself green, 98 test files / 1809 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed. TESTS/RUNNER-STORE-DAMAGE.TEST.TS REPRODUCED LATER IN THE SAME SESSION AND IS ALSO FIXED, BUT IT WAS NEVER THE SAME CAUSE. This entry first said there was no signature to work from, which was true when written — the file had just passed inside a concurrent full-suite run — and it failed on the next one. The issue's stated reason for grouping the two ('both start real child processes') is FALSE for this file: it spawns nothing and drives in-process HTTP servers over named pipes. THE SIGNATURE IS `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`, on exactly the two cases that call writeMalformedStore and on no others. 5000ms is vitest's DEFAULT testTimeout, so this is not a race: it is a fixture costing more than the default budget on a loaded machine, where solo it takes under two seconds. THE COST IS FOUR HUNDRED COMMITS AND NOT THE CORRUPTION. The fixture inserts 400 rows one at a time and every run() outside a transaction is its own commit; on journal_mode = DELETE — which the fixture sets deliberately, so that there is one file whose pages can be damaged — a commit means creating and deleting a rollback journal beside the database. 400 file-create/file-delete pairs is cheap on an idle machine and is not cheap on Windows with a filter driver watching the directory. One BEGIN/COMMIT around the loop changes NOTHING about the file produced — the same 400 rows land on the same pages, and the malformed-page overwrite afterwards is untouched — and it took the whole suite from 32.8s to 20.9s, which is how much of that time was journal round-trips inside one fixture. The explicit 30s budget on those two cases is the issue's own third preference applied on top: sized from the observed worst case rather than the median, said in a comment, roughly fifteen times the solo cost, and still short enough that a genuine hang fails the run rather than hanging it. THE GENERAL LESSON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: a test whose DEFAULT timeout is load-bearing is a flake with a countdown on it, and nothing in this suite distinguishes 'this assertion is fast' from 'this assertion has been fitting inside 5000ms so far'. Both halves of MAR-537 are the same failure at one remove — a harness making a bet about time, where the thing under test was never in question. issues.note: PLANNED 2026-08-16, PR open against master, commit to be filled by the coordinator at merge. THE OPENER HAD A SHELL IN IT AND A HANDOFF URL IS FULL OF AMMUNITION. `openUrl` spawned `cmd /c start "" <url>`; a handoff URL is dash://handoff?v=1&file=...&nonce=..., it contains no spaces so Node did not quote it, and cmd.exe treats every unquoted & as a COMMAND SEPARATOR. DASH was handed dash://handoff?v=1 with no file and no nonce and refused it correctly with 'That link does not say where the agent is.' Percent was the next mine along the same path: a percent-encoded Windows path is full of %3A and %5C and cmd expands those too. Quoting the URL would have fixed today and left the parser in the path, so cmd is GONE: openCommand returns rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler <url>, which is ShellExecute and nothing else — all `start` was ever wanted for. WHY THIS SURVIVED MAR-428'S PROOF: nothing regularly exercised reaches openUrl. 'Try a sample agent' builds the handoff inside DASH and calls openHandoff directly, so the seeded first-run journey never touched cmd. The only caller is the Agent Kit's own terminal path, which is the first thing a developer who is not Henrik ever runs. THE DECISION IS NOW PLATFORM-PARAMETERISED so a posix CI runner can assert the Windows argument vector — a Windows-only bug guarded by a Windows-only test is a test that does not run. TWO KINDS OF ASSERTION, deliberately: tests/open-in-dash-url.test.ts checks that no shell appears in the vector on any of the three platforms and that the URL is one intact final argument, and then spawns a REAL CHILD PROCESS with the same spawn options and reads back what it received byte for byte. The old shape was untestable in the way that mattered — it spawned and unreffed, so nothing could observe the URL surviving. PROVEN ON THIS MACHINE, at the OS level rather than by inference: `npm run open-in-dash` from the competitor scout's folder, with a WMI poll capturing new process command lines, caught electron.exe launched with the whole URL — & and % intact — as a single argument. The single-instance lock is keyed on userData, so the deep-link copy collided with nothing and opened a WHOLE SECOND DASH with its own store, its own runner and its own agents. It had been collecting them since 2026-08-03. assertStoreLocation ran on every one of those launches and passed, because it compared the resolved store against app.getPath('userData') and IN THE PHANTOM BOTH SIDES SAID Electron — equality with yourself is not identity, which is why the new check is against a constant. THE GATE ON app.setName IS THE SUBTLE PART AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The first shape of this fix set the name for every importer of main.ts, and that would have broken a dozen capture harnesses: they import ./main.js and deliberately do NOT import smoke-identity.ts, precisely so they run as `Electron` and can photograph DASH beside a live one without losing the single-instance lock to it. electron/capture-settings-polish.ts states the bargain in full. THE DECISION: the chief gets a model, and exactly ONE of the two locks MAR-648 recorded moves. broker.handle's first parameter becomes a BrokerPrincipal union ({kind:'agent';agent_id} | {kind:'chief'}) rather than an agent id string -- a type and not a reserved string, because lib/handoff.ts and lib/open-link.ts both accept /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/ and 'dash.fleet' satisfies it, so a string comparison inside the broker would be a hole an agent author could aim at by choosing a name. readManifest answers for the chief with a manifest DASH composes from lib/fleet/catalogue.ts carrying ONE connection and ONE capability ({provider}.chat.completion) -- not a new authority, because ADR 0013 already granted DASH the right to decide what a fleet connection asks for and derived it from the frozen operation table. connectionSecretName DOES NOT MOVE: it goes on emitting dash.connection. and is never called for a chief, which calls fleetSecretName instead, so lib/fleet/principal.ts's sentence -- no agent, named anything at all, resolves to the fleet credential's vault key -- survives verbatim and is now true for two independent reasons. ADR 0013's rejected alternative ('the broker reads the fleet key directly') is amended and scoped to a principal that is not an agent; both its stated reasons were about agents and neither reaches here. NEW INVARIANT: the chief can ask a model a question and be charged for it and can do nothing else. Origin stays 'person' (ADR 0016 untouched, an unattended chief spend is unreachable rather than refused); model is DASH's fleet default with no picker of its own (ADR 0012 decision 4 untouched); the answer still drives nothing. FACTS VS PHRASING, ANSWERED HONESTLY: describeChief's never-reworded rule DOES NOT survive 'which agents run local vs cloud', because that is a join over records and not a quote of one. It is replaced by the briefing rule (every field sent is a string DASH already renders on a screen) plus a receipt rendered from DASH's own records rather than parsed out of the answer -- AskCitation's discipline moved to fleet facts -- plus records-first: answerChief and STANDING_WORDS stay in front, so the most-asked question stays free, instant and exact. What the receipt does NOT prevent is named: a model can still attribute a fact to the wrong agent or drop one, and no test catches that. MEMORY: the session-only argument is answered, not ignored -- it was an argument against undated re-presentation, so the transcript becomes durable (chief_messages beside agent_questions, ADR 0012's own precedent) with the receipt frozen alongside it and a staleness marker computed by comparing two of DASH's own records; the model is told only the last few turns and NEVER an old receipt. No vector store, no embeddings: the chief's memory is conversational continuity, its knowledge is always fresh. VOICE: small talk rides the same call with an empty briefing, never a canned-greeting table, and its receipt says nothing from your records was used. ROOM SCOPE: enforced by the type -- {kind:'chief'} carries no agent id, so no chief question can be aimed at an agent and no agent question can carry the fleet briefing. MODEL RECOMMENDATION: the fleet default, and set it to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001; the consequence that Anthropic does not price its own answers is stated. VISUALS: zero corners HELD. 'Softer' is diagnosed as border count and density, not radius -- .chief-asked's accent bar, .chief-quoted's second rule, .chief-reply at --text-sm so the answer is smaller than the question, and .chief-room a bordered box inside a bordered band. Unbox the turns, return to base size, one accent, keep the square corners. An exception would be a declared one across app/tokens.css and tests/tokens.test.ts and this ADR recommends not spending it yet. SEQUENCING: the boundary, the receipt, the transcript and the visual pass are provable before MAR-647; whether the briefing is ENOUGH, whether phrasing stays faithful, what a question costs, and the hand-off end to end are NOT judgeable until the competitor scout has produced real work -- Henrik's own 'the agents have no real output so we can't really test this'. That absence IS the finding, and it is what the hardening fixes. RULED OUT WITH EVIDENCE, all three pinned as tests: (a) rename window -- set() writes <target>.tmp, verifies it decrypts, then renameSync onto the name, so the target is never absent; pinned by reading the directory from inside encryptString, the exact moment a window would be open. issues.note: PLANNED 2026-08-25: per-schedule spend allowance, ADR 0029 AMENDMENT 1 (not a new ADR). Worktree wt-spend-allowance-j1, branch 000henrik/mar-784-spend-allowance, cut from origin/master c516fa0. MIGRATION INDEX 34 -> user_version 35, assigned as 34 and CONFIRMED AGAINST THE LITERAL PIN in tests/store-sqlite.test.ts at the branch point BEFORE it was written (pin read 34, so the next index is 34 and it produces 35). WHAT SHIPS, on Henrik's ruling on decision 6 ("Sure, but can we have the option to opt out on this. Some agents really need to use AI and some don't"): agent_schedules.allowance_calls + agent_schedule_runs.allowance_calls, both defaulting to 0, so every schedule already in an installed store keeps ADR 0029 decision 6 exactly. The ceiling on the ceiling is SPEND_ALLOWANCE_CALLS BY IDENTITY (MAX_SCHEDULE_ALLOWANCE_CALLS *is* that constant) so an unattended run can never be worth more than the press of Run now it stands in for, and openRunSpend clamps to the same number on the far side of the seam -- down, never up. The panel offers a SWITCH, not a number field; the column stays numeric so offering the quantity later is a control rather than a migration. THE SEAM, AND THE DESIGN DECISION WORTH READING: the runner does NOT enforce and CANNOT spend -- it holds no broker, no key, no provider, unchanged. What it gained is one sentence only it can say ("I started this agent, at this moment, under a schedule carrying this ceiling"), carried as a ScheduledAllowance ON THE REPLY TO POST /broker/drain rather than a route of its own. That is the safety argument: DASH's broker loop and its evidence poll are two independent timers, so a ceiling delivered on one and a request drained by the other would sometimes arrive AFTER the request it covers -- a scheduled run refused at 03:00 for a reason nobody can reproduce at nine. In one reply there is no ordering to get wrong. A FIRE ID makes the repeated report safe: allowRunSpend REPLACES rather than tops up, and the runner must keep reporting a live ceiling (a failed drain must not cost somebody their run), so without an identity per fire the ceiling would refresh to full several times a minute and stop being a ceiling. electron/broker-host.ts opens each fire_id exactly once and grants min(reported, stored), refusing outright if the schedule has since been switched off -- so the wire can only NARROW what the person set on their own page. THE COST, STATED ON THE PANEL AND NOT ONLY IN THE ADR: a scheduled run spends only WHILE DASH IS OPEN. That is not new and this packet does not worsen it -- electron/broker-host.ts has said since MAR-458 that when DASH is not running the broker is not running, and locally an agent's brokered requests are BUFFERED by the runner for DASH to drain, so with DASH closed a model step has always settled as broker_unavailable after the template's 30s BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS. What is new is that the ceiling makes the boundary visible, so a fourth sentence sits beside the three liveness ones: "That works while DASH is open. With DASH closed the run still starts and still publishes, but nothing can reach your model until you open DASH again." WHAT WOULD LIFT THAT, NAMED AND NOT BUILT: a broker in the runner holding a model key, narrowed the way runner/chief-broker.ts is for the chief and runner/host-broker.ts is for a host. It needs a credential route, per-agent model resolution in main, an audit drain, and -- the part that makes it a DECISION rather than a task -- a model key in a second process for EVERY scheduled agent, which is the widening ADR 0028 decision 5 argued once for ONE key. That argument has to be made again at the new size before anybody makes it. HENRIK WAS ASKED WHICH SHAPE TO BUILD AND DID NOT ANSWER; the bounded one was built under a stated assumption and the ADR amendment records it. THE DEGRADE: a run that spends its allowance gets needs_a_person on the next model step -- THE SAME REFUSAL, BY THE SAME CODE PATH, a schedule with no allowance gets today, because spendAllowed deliberately cannot tell absent/expired/spent apart (an agent must not be able to learn the shape of a budget by probing it). So there is no new failure mode: the agent stops asking, finishes without a model, publishes what it could. RECEIPTS ARE COUNTED, NOT REPORTED: no spent_calls column, because a run's end reaches DASH as an event the AGENT emits and a count written from it would be the party being reported on doing the reporting. readScheduleSpend scans broker_audit over the allowance window (refusals included, resolved through operationById + isSpendOperation rather than a LIKE on the id, which would have counted one of the three spend operations and missed two). The panel says "Used 1 of 2 model calls." and, ONLY WHEN A CALL WAS ACTUALLY REFUSED, that the run used them all and still published -- never when used === allowed, because an agent that needed exactly its two calls and asked for no third was not cut short. STATED IMPRECISION: a press of Run now within ten minutes of a fire lands in the same window; broker_audit records which agent and which operation, never which press, and a request that could name its own press is what BrokerOrigin exists to refuse. FOLLOW-UPS STILL OPEN: the runner-side broker above; restart-on-boot (ADR 0007); cron; weekly/every-N-hours; more than one schedule per agent; MAR-588's Discord message still does not say a run was scheduled.
